charter.json.title: Professional Services Restriction
charter.json.rationale: California does not permit an LLC to render professional services requiring a license. This is a formation-blocking issue, not a drafting preference.
charter.json.body: California law does not permit a {{entityLong}} to render professional services for which a license is required. If any service the Company intends to provide in {{opStateLong}} requires a state license, the Company must be organized as a professional corporation or a registered limited liability partnership instead. Confirm the licensing status of every intended service line before filing.

compliance-calendar.json.title: California Statement of Information
compliance-calendar.json.rationale: Due within 90 days of registration and easy to miss because it is separate from the formation filing itself.
compliance-calendar.json.body: California requires an initial Statement of Information within 90 days of formation or registration — that is {{soiDeadline}} for this Company — and {{caSoiRenewal}}, filed during an applicable filing period made up of the calendar month in which the original articles were filed and the five calendar months immediately before it. The Secretary of State sends a reminder about three months before that period closes, and not receiving it is not an excuse. If the statement is not filed, the Secretary of State first sends a notice of delinquency; only if nothing is filed within 60 days of that notice does it certify the Company to the Franchise Tax Board, which then assesses a penalty of two hundred fifty dollars ($250). The Secretary of State may waive that penalty for reasonable cause or unusual circumstances justifying the failure. Suspension is a further step and not the ordinary consequence of one late filing: a corporation becomes subject to it only if it failed to file for the period, has filed no statement for the preceding 24 months, and was certified for the penalty for that same period — and even then a second 60-day notice runs first. While suspended, a corporation's powers, rights, and privileges are suspended except to apply for exempt status or to amend its articles as needed to perfect that application or take a new name, and the courts have held it cannot prosecute or defend a lawsuit in that condition. It may still file the statement; on filing, the Secretary of State certifies that to the Franchise Tax Board and the corporation may be relieved from suspension unless the Board holds it suspended for tax reasons.

employment.json.title: Meal Period Policy
employment.json.rationale: California meal period violations carry a one-hour premium per day and are among the most frequently litigated wage claims.
employment.json.body: A non-exempt employee may not be employed for a work period of more than five (5) hours per day without being provided a meal period of not less than thirty (30) minutes, nor for more than ten (10) hours per day without a second period of not less than thirty (30) minutes. Because the duty attaches to a work period of more than five hours, the first period has to be provided before the fifth hour is complete. The first period may be waived by mutual consent of the Company and the employee where the total work period for the day is no more than six (6) hours; the second may be waived by mutual consent where the total hours worked is no more than twelve (12) hours and the first was not waived. The Company's duty is to relieve the employee of all duty for the period and relinquish control over how the time is spent; it is not a duty to ensure that no work is done, so a compliant period the employee chooses to work through owes nothing. A period during which the employee is not relieved of all duty is an on-duty meal period, counted as time worked, and is permitted only where the nature of the work prevents relief from all duty and the parties have signed a written agreement stating that the employee may revoke it in writing at any time. Where a compliant meal period is not provided, one (1) additional hour of pay is owed for that workday at the employee's regular rate of compensation — which means the same thing as the regular rate of pay used for overtime, and so takes in non-discretionary payments and not the base hourly rate alone. Meal periods must be recorded and those punches may not be rounded; records showing a missed, short or delayed period raise a rebuttable presumption of a violation, which the Company can meet with evidence that a compliant period was provided or the premium paid. Section 512 does not reach employees in certain occupations covered by a qualifying collective bargaining agreement, or the motion picture and broadcasting agreements described in the section.

employment.json.title: Rest Period Policy
employment.json.rationale: Rest periods are paid time and cannot be combined with meal periods or used to leave early. The premium is the same one hour per day.
employment.json.body: The Company authorizes and permits non-exempt employees to take rest periods, which insofar as practicable shall be in the middle of each work period. Rest time is based on total hours worked daily at the rate of ten (10) minutes net rest time per four (4) hours or major fraction thereof: ten minutes for a shift of three and one-half to six hours, twenty minutes for more than six and up to ten hours, thirty minutes for more than ten and up to fourteen, and so on. No rest period need be authorized where the employee's total daily work time is less than three and one-half (3½) hours. Rest periods are counted as hours worked and there is no deduction from wages for them. A rest period must be off duty: the Company must relieve the employee of all duties and relinquish control over how the time is spent, and may not require the employee to remain on call. Where a rest period is not provided, one (1) additional hour of pay is owed for that workday at the employee's regular rate of compensation, which takes in non-discretionary payments and not the base hourly rate alone. Rest periods are scheduled so that they are not combined with a meal period or taken in exchange for leaving early — NOT VERIFIED: no provision of Wage Order No. 4-2001 or the Labor Code read for this rebuild states that rule, and it is carried here as Company practice following from the "middle of each work period" requirement, not as a legal requirement. The Legislature has displaced the off-duty rule for a registered security officer employed by a registered private patrol operator under a qualifying collective bargaining agreement, who may be required to remain on the premises and on call; that exception reaches no other occupation.

employment.json.title: PTO Accrual
employment.json.rationale: Accrued vacation is wages in California. A use-it-or-lose-it policy is unenforceable and creates a wage claim at every departure.
employment.json.body: Accrued and unused vacation is wages under California law and is paid out at termination at the final rate of pay. The Company does not operate a use-it-or-lose-it policy; accrual may be capped at a reasonable multiple of the annual accrual rate but may not be forfeited.

employment.json.title: Final Pay Timing
employment.json.rationale: California waiting time penalties accrue at a full day of wages per day late, up to thirty days, for a payroll timing error alone.
employment.json.body: An employee who is discharged must be paid all wages earned and unpaid immediately at the time of discharge. An employee who quits must be paid within seventy-two (72) hours, or at the time of quitting if they gave seventy-two hours' previous notice; an employee who quits without that notice may request payment by mail, and the date of mailing is then the date of payment. Final pay includes accrued vested vacation under <<xr:emp_pto>> and any meal or rest period premium owed, which is a wage for this purpose and not merely a penalty. Several groups are on their own clocks and are not covered by the general rule: a seasonal layoff in the curing, canning or drying of perishable fruit, fish or vegetables is payable within a reasonable time not exceeding seventy-two (72) hours; an oil drilling layoff within twenty-four (24) hours excluding Saturdays, Sundays and holidays; and temporary services, motion picture, print shoot and live theatrical or concert venue employees are governed by Labor Code sections 201.3, 201.5, 201.6 and 201.9. A wilful failure to pay makes the employee's wages continue as a penalty at the same daily rate until paid or until an action is commenced, and for no more than thirty (30) days. The penalty does not follow automatically from lateness: an employer that reasonably and in good faith disputes that the wages are due has not acted wilfully, and an employee who hides, avoids payment, or refuses a full tender takes no benefit for that time.

employment.json.title: Itemized Wage Statements
employment.json.rationale: Wage statement claims are commonly added to any other wage claim because the defect is visible on the face of the document.
employment.json.body: Every wage payment shall be accompanied by an itemized statement showing gross wages, total hours worked for non-exempt employees, all deductions, net wages, the pay period dates, the employee’s name and last four digits of their identification number, and the Company’s legal name and address as stated in <<xr:charter_name>>.

employment.json.title: Paid Sick Leave
employment.json.rationale: Paid sick leave is mandatory in both states at low employee counts, and the accrual and carryover mechanics differ from vacation.
employment.json.body: Employees accrue paid sick leave as required by the law of {{opStateLong}}, beginning on the first day of employment and available for use as provided by that law. Sick leave is tracked separately from vacation, and unused sick leave carries over subject to any statutory cap.

employment.json.title: Non-Compete Prohibition Notice
employment.json.rationale: Since AB 1076 it is unlawful to include or attempt to enforce a non-compete in California, and notice to affected current and former employees was required.
employment.json.body: The Company shall not require any employee working in California to sign a non-compete or customer non-solicitation covenant. Such provisions are void under California law regardless of where the agreement was signed or which state’s law it names. The Company protects its interests through the confidentiality and invention assignment obligations in <<xr:emp_ip>> instead.

equity.json.title: Statutory Invention Carve-Out
equity.json.rationale: California requires written notice of the statutory carve-out. An assignment that purports to cover more than the statute allows can be attacked as overbroad.
equity.json.body: This assignment does not apply to an invention that the founder developed entirely on their own time without using Company equipment, supplies, facilities, or trade secret information, except for an invention that either (a) relates, at the time of conception or reduction to practice, to the Company's business or to the Company's actual or demonstrably anticipated research or development, or (b) results from any work performed by the founder for the Company. To the extent a provision purports to require assignment of an invention that this carve-out excludes, it is against the public policy of California and is unenforceable, and the Company may not require such a provision as a condition of employment or continued employment. This written notification is given under California Labor Code §2872, which requires it whenever an employment agreement entered into after January 1, 1980 contains an invention-assignment provision; §2870 is the section that defines which inventions are excluded. In any suit or action, the person claiming the benefit of §2870 bears the burden of proof. Sections 2870 to 2872 speak to employees and employment agreements, and whether they reach a founder who is not an employee is a question this notice does not decide.

equity.json.title: Spousal Signature
equity.json.rationale: In a community property state the spouse may hold an interest in the shares, and the election is cleaner if they sign it too.
equity.json.body: If the undersigned is married and resides in a community property jurisdiction, the undersigned’s spouse should also sign this election with respect to any community property interest in the shares.

governance-transfers.json.title: Spousal Consent
governance-transfers.json.benchmark: Present in 51% of multi-owner agreements in community property states
governance-transfers.json.rationale: In a community property state a spouse may hold an interest in the ownership stake without ever signing anything. A consent makes the buy-sell enforceable against that interest.
governance-transfers.json.body: Each married {{ownerSing}} residing in a community property jurisdiction shall cause their spouse to execute the spousal consent attached as Exhibit B, acknowledging this {{govDoc}} and agreeing that any community property interest is bound by the transfer restrictions in <<xr:gov_transfer>> and the buy-sell provisions in <<xr:gov_buysell>>.

hiring.json.title: No Non-Compete
hiring.json.rationale: Since AB 1076 it is unlawful to include or attempt to enforce a non-compete against a California employee, regardless of the governing law the agreement names.
hiring.json.body: This agreement contains no non-compete or customer non-solicitation covenant. Such provisions are void under California law and it is unlawful to include or attempt to enforce them, regardless of where the agreement is signed or which state’s law it names. The Company relies on the confidentiality and invention assignment obligations in <<xr:ea_ip>> instead.

hiring.json.title: Meal and Rest Periods
hiring.json.rationale: California meal and rest violations each carry a one-hour premium per day, and they are the most frequently litigated wage claims in the state.
hiring.json.body: If you are non-exempt you are entitled to an unpaid, uninterrupted meal period of at least thirty (30) minutes when you work more than five (5) hours in a day, and to a second one when you work more than ten (10) hours. The first has to be provided before your fifth hour is complete. You and the Company may agree to waive the first period on a day when you will work no more than six (6) hours, and to waive the second on a day of no more than twelve (12) hours if you did not waive the first. What the Company owes is to relieve you of all duty and leave you free to use the time as you like; it does not have to police the break, so a break you were given and chose to work through does not entitle you to extra pay. You are also authorized and permitted paid rest periods of ten (10) minutes for every four (4) hours worked or major fraction, which works out to ten minutes on a shift of three and one-half to six hours, twenty minutes over six and up to ten, and thirty minutes over ten and up to fourteen; no rest period is required on a shift under three and one-half hours. A rest period is off duty — the Company cannot ask you to stay on call through it — and is paid time. On any workday you are not provided a compliant meal period, and again on any workday you are not provided a compliant rest period, you are owed one (1) additional hour of pay at your regular rate of compensation, which is the same measure as the regular rate used for overtime and includes non-discretionary payments, not just your base hourly rate. That premium is a wage, so it is also reportable on your wage statement and payable when your employment ends.
